Uriah Heep. The obsequious and hypocritical clerk in David Copperfield whose false humility and greasy manner conceal ruthless ambition and malevolence. He works as a clerk to Mr. Wickfield and gradually insinuates himself into a position of authority through a combination of slavish deference and blackmail. He constantly refers to himself as "humble" and "umble," using exaggerated courtesy and hand-wringing as a weapon to disarm suspicion. Beneath this pose lies a passionate, possessive desire for Agnes Wickfield, which he uses to pressure her as his growing control over her father's affairs deepens. His true nature is revealed when David discovers that Heep has forged documents, embezzled funds, and coerced both Micawber and Wickfield into complicity. Even after his crimes are exposed and he is imprisoned, he maintains his contemptible pose of injured humility. He represents Dickens' warning against judging by appearances and his contempt for false piety masking greed and cruelty.
